findings.text: the log negative_control_log names attests revision 0a5766aa plus the node's previous head change and runs a three-case copy of the test file, so it does not attest the promoted commit; the negative-control run for 77ef0c137390 (1 failed, 3 passed, reddening tests/test_an_exited_worker_under_a_live_supervisor_reads_halted.py:181) was piped through `tail -8` and stored nowhere, so the record cites a red log produced from other code than the code it lands.

the artifacts line states the added set is zero and the fixed set is empty, while the baseline_suite and after_suite receipts the same record carries give 9 added and 2 fixed ids (16 failed at head against 9 failed at base, set difference computed from logs/population_head.log and the mon69 base.log), so a reader taking the artifact figure concludes the population arm added nothing.

the base arm runs at revision 2998d0bd59, 67 commits ahead of the node's own base 0a5766aa on the merge lineage and containing no node commit, so the nine head-only ids may come from the head tree lacking those 67 commits rather than from this node's change; settling the added set needs the arm at 0a5766aa, which the manifest's checkpoint already names as remaining work.

the new case sets the worker record's pid and the similar exit record's worker_pid to the same live process, so a reading of the worker record's pid in place of the exit record's own worker_pid survives all four cases and the guard does not pin which source it names.
